title: 5 Design Decisions that make Linear feel 'Expensive'
summary: This reel reverse-engineers the design of the Linear app, highlighting five specific UI decisions that contribute to its premium feel. It covers information density, the use of borders over shadows, minimal color palettes, keyboard-first interactions, and strict alignment.

transcript.text: Why does Linear feel expensive? Five decisions. No designer.
Decision 1: Density. 13 pixel text. 32 pixel rows. Letter spacing pulled in 1%. Twice the issues on one screen, no scroll. Density reads as competence.

Decision 2: Borders, not shadows. A 1 pixel border at 8% white. Depth comes from three background values, not blur. Hover changes the surface value, not the elevation. Flat surfaces look engineered. Shadows look decorated.
Decision 3: One color. Indigo on the selected row and the primary button, nowhere else. Status is an icon, not a colored pill. Everything else sits in gray.

Decision 4: Keyboard. Every action shows its shortcut. C creates, Command K searches. Hover feedback in 80 milliseconds, transitions under 150. No bounce, no overshoot. The UI answers before you finish the gesture.
Decision 5: Alignment. A 4 pixel grid. 16 pixel icons centered on the text. Labels left, numbers right, nothing centered. Alignment is invisible when right, loud when wrong.
Five decisions, one afternoon. Or type /restyle. UX Engine, the Claude code plugin that makes your app look this deliberate. Link in bio.
